title: litter
intro:
Litter, surface residuals, or mulch below canopy.
   < component        >

Log Variables
    cover : number [<fraction>]
     Fraction of surface area covered by litter.

attrs.name: cover
attrs.doc: Fraction of surface area covered by litter.

sections.name: none
sections.desc: The effect of surface residuals is ignored by the model.
sections.text:
The effect of surface residuals is ignored by the model.
   Used by column default Litter (see 26.1, page 153) .

sections.name: permanent
sections.desc: A permanent litter layer cover the ground, as for example in a forest.
sections.sig:
< permanent (albedo albedo )
                  (vapor flux factor 1 [<fraction>])
                  (interception capacity interception capacity ) >

attrs.name: albedo
attrs.doc: Reflection factor. By default, the surface albedo will be used.

attrs.name: vapor flux factor
attrs.doc: Reduction factor for potential evaporation below litter.

attrs.name: interception capacity
attrs.doc: Storage capacity of litter.

sections.text:
A permanent litter layer cover the ground, as for example in a forest.
  < permanent (albedo albedo )
                  (vapor flux factor 1 [<fraction>])
                  (interception capacity interception capacity ) >

    albedo: number (dimensionless)
     Optional parameter
     Reflection factor. By default, the surface albedo will be used.

    vapor flux factor : number [<fraction>]
     Parameter (default 1)
     Reduction factor for potential evaporation below litter.

    interception capacity: number [mm]
     Parameter
     Storage capacity of litter.

sections.name: residue
sections.desc:
A dynamic litter layer based on applied fertilizer and crop residuals.
    A ’mulch area index’ is calculated from the surface organic matericals, and from
that a mulch cover is calculated based on Beer’s law similarily to how the crop cover
is calculated from the leaf area index. See also [Scopel et al., 2004]
sections.sig:
< residue        (albedo albedo )
                   (vapor flux factor 0 [<fraction>])
                   (water capacity water capacity )
                   (specific AI specific AI )
                   (extinction coefficent extinction coefficent ) >

attrs.name: albedo
attrs.doc: Reflection factor. By default, the surface albedo will be used.

attrs.name: vapor flux factor
attrs.doc:
Reduction factor for potential evaporation below litter. Only area covered by
        residue is affected.

attrs.name: water capacity
attrs.doc: Water holding capacity of surface residulas.

attrs.name: specific AI
attrs.doc: Area covered per litter mass.

attrs.name: extinction coefficent
attrs.doc:
Beer’s law extinction coefficient for litter.
Log Variables

attrs.name: mass
attrs.doc: Total mass of mulch layer.

sections.name: mulch
sections.desc:
A ‘residue’ model (see 51.3, page 275) build into Daisy.
   A decomposing mulch layer.
   The bottom of the mulch layer may decompose based on the conditions in the
top of soil. See also [Findeling et al., 2007]
sections.sig:
< mulch     (alpha 0 [])
             (retention retention )                            ; Default PASTIS value.
             (T ref 10 [dg C])
             (decompose heat factor decompose heat factor )    ; Has default value.
             (decompose water factor decompose water factor )  ; Has default value.
             (decompose SMB pool 1)
             (decompose SMB KM 0 [g C/cm3 ])
             (SMB ref SMB ref )
             (DOC name DOC)
             (DON name DON)
             (density density )
             (Theta res Theta res )
             (particle density particle density )
             (decompose height decompose height )
             (evaporate depth 1000 [cm])
             (soil height soil height )
             (h min -3.16228e+06 [cm])
             (factor exch factor exch )
             (Si Si )
             (use soil decompose true)
             ;; Shared parameters are described in section 51.3.
             (albedo albedo )
             (vapor flux factor 0 [<fraction>])
             (water capacity water capacity )
             (specific AI specific AI )
             (extinction coefficent extinction coefficent ) >

attrs.name: alpha
attrs.doc:
Interception parameter. The fraction of water hitting the litter will be deter-
    mined by:
    exp (-alpha (Theta sat - Theta res) / (Theta sat - Theta))
    If alpha is 0 (default), all water hitting the canopy will be intercepted.

attrs.name: retention
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘PASTIS’)
    The retention curve to use.

attrs.name: T ref
attrs.doc:
Reference temperature for decomposition. The heat factor on decomposition
    will be scaled so it is 1 at this temperature..

attrs.name: decompose heat factor
attrs.doc: Heat factor on decomposition.

attrs.name: decompose water factor
attrs.doc: Water potential factor on decomposition.

attrs.name: decompose SMB pool
attrs.doc:
SMB pool for Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Use 0 for SMB1, 1 for SMB2, or -1
    for all SMB pools.

attrs.name: decompose SMB KM
attrs.doc:
Michaelis-Menten kinetics parameter. Decompose rate is modified by C /
        (KM + C), where C is the carbon content in the pool specified by ’decom-
        pose SMB pool’.

attrs.name: SMB ref
attrs.doc:
Reference SMB carbon for docomposition of mulch. The SMB factor for
        decomposition will be scaled so it is 1 at this amount of SMB carbon. By
        default, it will not be scaled.

attrs.name: DOC name
attrs.doc: Name of compound representing dissolved organic carbon.

attrs.name: DON name
attrs.doc: Name of compound representing dissolved organic nitrogen.

attrs.name: density
attrs.doc: Bulk density of mulch layer.

attrs.name: Theta res
attrs.doc: Water content where biological activity stops

attrs.name: particle density
attrs.doc: Particle density of mulch layer. If unspecified, use bulk density instead.

attrs.name: decompose height
attrs.doc:
Height of muclh layer considered in contact with the soil. Only this part of
        the mulch layer will decompose

attrs.name: evaporate depth
attrs.doc:
Depth into mulch layer affected by evaporation. Only water in this part of
        the mulch layer will evaporate.
        The mulch layer is asumed to be filled up from the bottom.
        If W is the amount of water in the mulch, R is the residual water (Theta res
        * C), C is the water capacity, D is this parameter, and H is the height of the
        mulch layer, the maximum evaporation (Ea max) can be found as:
        Ea max = max (0, (W - R) - (C - R) * (H - min (D, H)) / H)

attrs.name: soil height
attrs.doc: Height of soil layer (a negative number) contributing to decay.

attrs.name: h min
attrs.doc: Water pressure where biological activity stops.

attrs.name: factor exch
attrs.doc:
Limiting factor when calculating Darcy exchange between mulch and soil. It
    is intended to emulate poor contact between the two media.

attrs.name: Si
attrs.doc:
Water content where diffusion to wash off begins relative to Theta sat. Theta sat
    = 100 %

attrs.name: use soil decompose
attrs.doc:
Use temperature and moisture of top soil for turnover and decomposition.
    The depth of the top soil is determined by ’soil height’.

sections.text:
A ‘residue’ model (see 51.3, page 275) build into Daisy.
   A decomposing mulch layer.
   The bottom of the mulch layer may decompose based on the conditions in the
top of soil. See also [Findeling et al., 2007]

 < mulch     (alpha 0 [])
             (retention retention )                            ; Default PASTIS value.
             (T ref 10 [dg C])
             (decompose heat factor decompose heat factor )    ; Has default value.
             (decompose water factor decompose water factor )  ; Has default value.
             (decompose SMB pool 1)
             (decompose SMB KM 0 [g C/cm3 ])
             (SMB ref SMB ref )
             (DOC name DOC)
             (DON name DON)
             (density density )
             (Theta res Theta res )
             (particle density particle density )
             (decompose height decompose height )
             (evaporate depth 1000 [cm])
             (soil height soil height )
             (h min -3.16228e+06 [cm])
             (factor exch factor exch )
             (Si Si )
             (use soil decompose true)
             ;; Shared parameters are described in section 51.3.
             (albedo albedo )
             (vapor flux factor 0 [<fraction>])
             (water capacity water capacity )
             (specific AI specific AI )
             (extinction coefficent extinction coefficent ) >

   alpha: number (dimensionless)
    Parameter (default 0)
    Interception parameter. The fraction of water hitting the litter will be deter-
    mined by:
    exp (-alpha (Theta sat - Theta res) / (Theta sat - Theta))
    If alpha is 0 (default), all water hitting the canopy will be intercepted.

   retention: retention component (see chapter 71)
    Component (default ‘PASTIS’)
    The retention curve to use.

   T ref : number [dg C]
    Parameter (default 10)
    Reference temperature for decomposition. The heat factor on decomposition
    will be scaled so it is 1 at this temperature..

   decompose heat factor : plf [dg C → <none>]
    Parameter (has default value with 0 points)
    Heat factor on decomposition.

   decompose water factor : plf [cm → <none>]
    Parameter (has default value with 0 points)
    Water potential factor on decomposition.

   decompose SMB pool : integer
    Parameter (default 1)
    SMB pool for Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Use 0 for SMB1, 1 for SMB2, or -1
    for all SMB pools.

       decompose SMB KM : number [g C/cm3 ]
        Parameter (default 0)
        Michaelis-Menten kinetics parameter. Decompose rate is modified by C /
        (KM + C), where C is the carbon content in the pool specified by ’decom-
        pose SMB pool’.

       SMB ref : number [g C/cm3 ]
        Optional parameter
        Reference SMB carbon for docomposition of mulch. The SMB factor for
        decomposition will be scaled so it is 1 at this amount of SMB carbon. By
        default, it will not be scaled.

       DOC name: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Parameter (default ‘DOC’)
        Name of compound representing dissolved organic carbon.

       DON name: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Parameter (default ‘DON’)
        Name of compound representing dissolved organic nitrogen.

       density: number [kg DM/m3 ]
        Parameter
        Bulk density of mulch layer.

       Theta res: number (dimensionless)
        Parameter
        Water content where biological activity stops

       particle density: number [kg DM/m3 ]
        Optional parameter
        Particle density of mulch layer. If unspecified, use bulk density instead.

       decompose height: number [cm]
        Parameter
        Height of muclh layer considered in contact with the soil. Only this part of
        the mulch layer will decompose

       evaporate depth: number [cm]
        Parameter (default 1000)
        Depth into mulch layer affected by evaporation. Only water in this part of
        the mulch layer will evaporate.
        The mulch layer is asumed to be filled up from the bottom.
        If W is the amount of water in the mulch, R is the residual water (Theta res
        * C), C is the water capacity, D is this parameter, and H is the height of the
        mulch layer, the maximum evaporation (Ea max) can be found as:
        Ea max = max (0, (W - R) - (C - R) * (H - min (D, H)) / H)

       soil height: number [cm]
        Parameter
        Height of soil layer (a negative number) contributing to decay.

       h min: number [cm]
        Parameter (default -3.16228e+06)
        Water pressure where biological activity stops.

   factor exch: number (dimensionless)
    Parameter
    Limiting factor when calculating Darcy exchange between mulch and soil. It
    is intended to emulate poor contact between the two media.

   Si : number [<fraction>]
    Parameter
    Water content where diffusion to wash off begins relative to Theta sat. Theta sat
    = 100 %

   use soil decompose: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
    Parameter (default true)
    Use temperature and moisture of top soil for turnover and decomposition.
    The depth of the top soil is determined by ’soil height’.

Log Variables
   h: number [cm]
    Mulch water potential at stat of timestep.

   water : number [mm]
    Total water in mulch.

   Theta: number (dimensionless)
    Relative water content.

   factor : number (dimensionless)
    The combined effect of SMB, T, h, and contact. This affects both turnover
    and chemical decomposition in litter.

   T : number [dg C]
    Temperature of water in mulch.

   h factor : number (dimensionless)
    Water potential effect on turnover.

   T factor : number (dimensionless)
    Temperature effect on turnover.

   SMB C : number [g C/cm3 ]
    Microbical C in top soil.

   height: number [cm]
    Total height of mulch layer.

   contact: number [<fraction>]
    Fraction of mulch layer in contact with soil. DOM in this part of the mulch
    is degraded.

   protected water : number [mm]
    Amount of water potentially protected from evaporation. Only when the
    water content exceeds this amount it will evaporate.

   h1 : number [cm]
    Estimated mulch water potential at end of timestep.

   h soil : number [cm]
    Soil water potential.

       K soil : number [cm/h]
        Soil water conductivity.
       E darcy: number [cm/h]
        Potential mulch-soil water exchange as calculated by modified Darcy. Positive
        down.
       T soil : number [dg C]
        Temperature of top soil.

       SMB factor : number (dimensionless)
        Microbical effect on turnover.
       DOC gen: number [g/cm2 /h]
        Dissolved organic carbon generated from turnover.
       DON gen: number [g/cm2 /h]
        Dissolved organic nitrogen generated from turnover.
       SOC gen: number [g/cm2 /h]
        Stationary organic carbon generated from turnover.
       SON gen: number [g/cm2 /h]
        Stationary organic nitrogen generated from turnover.
